chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

It is written in the Torah among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Conceal the hidden aspect of My secret in your inner self, and manifest politeness on My behalf in your public appearances to My enemy and your enemy from My creation, and do not become presumptuous for Me in their presence by manifesting the hidden aspect of My secret, lest your enemy and My enemy participate in insulting Me.'

key_terms.مَكْتُومَ سِرِّي: The hidden/concealed aspect of My secret

ai.seo_question: What does the Torah say about how Prophet Musa should handle God's secret?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cites a passage from the Torah where God instructs Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) on the etiquette of divine secrecy. God commands Musa to keep His secret concealed in his inner self while displaying polite deference (al-mudarāh) in public to His and Musa's enemies, ensuring that their mockery does not lead to insulting God by revealing the secret prematurely. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of *al-mudarāh* (strategic dissimulation or politeness) as a means of preserving dignity and avoiding unnecessary conflict, reflecting the broader theme of balancing inner truth with outer social harmony.
